trust_decision.summary: Operator endpoints that run local subprocesses and return their output must be authenticated and fail closed: an HTTP middleware in scripts/aetherbrowser/api_server.py rejects every /api/ops/* and /api/cli/* request unless X-Admin-Token matches a configured SCBE_OPS_ADMIN_TOKEN (or SCBE_RUNTIME_GATE_ADMIN_TOKEN), and returns 403 when no token is configured at all. The decision is made globally, in front of the handlers, not inside them. BLOCKER FOR THIS CANDIDATE: the pinned tree does not contain the module at all. scripts/aetherbrowser/api_server.py is created as a new file by ca833795, one of the two listed fix commits (fix.diff:575-580), and the pinned PWA page is still the earlier 'AetherBrowser Mobile V1' stub whose backend calls are unwired (kindle-app/www/aetherbrowser.html:1357-1358, kindle-app/www/aetherbrowser.html:1230). The second fix commit de7779 is based on a much later revision (its context imports StaticFiles/Request, references /runtime-gate/checkpoint, and it patches scripts/hooks/pre-commit, none of which exist at the pinned commit). So at f57e3f73 there is no vulnerable route, no guard, and nothing for a solver to fix; the pinned commit is the parent of the feature commit that introduced the surface, not the parent of the security fix.

landing_point.why: The advisory names one concrete symptom: the ops email-digest endpoint. An engineer reading only the summary opens POST /api/ops/check-email and its handler, which shells out to scripts/apollo/email_reader.py and returns stdout. That location exists only inside the fix diff; at the pinned commit the whole file scripts/aetherbrowser/api_server.py is absent (created new by fix.diff:575-580), so the landing point resolves to nothing in the checked-out tree.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP middleware in front of every /api/ops/* and /api/cli/* route; the reported one is POST /api/ops/check-email (fix.diff:1196)
PWA Ops tab buttons -> POST /api/ops/check-email, /api/ops/youtube-review, /api/ops/tor-sweep, /api/ops/run-tests and GET /api/ops/git-status, /api/vault/stats (kindle-app/www/aetherbrowser.html)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists at the pinned commit; in the post-feature tree the dismissable argument would be that /api/vault/sync and /api/red-team/run are ordinary Vault/Rooms features, not operator endpoints, so the /api/ops/ guard need not cover them.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: CORS preflight must keep working for the cross-origin PWA: every request from the page to http://localhost:8100 is preceded by an OPTIONS preflight (allow_origins=["*"] at fix.diff:688-694), so a guard that rejects all unauthenticated or all non-GET requests to /api/ops/* breaks the Ops tab. A guard that bans every subprocess-running route also breaks the legitimate Vault stats and Red-Team suites tabs.

O6_input_shapes: correct token supplied via the SCBE_RUNTIME_GATE_ADMIN_TOKEN fallback
no token configured at all -> 403 fail closed (endpoints disabled)
OPTIONS preflight exempt from the check
path-prefix match on /api/ops/ and /api/cli/ rather than enumerating individual routes

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an /api/ops/* subprocess route added directly to the existing AetherBrowser FastAPI app instead of to a new api_server.py module
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: src/aetherbrowser/serve.py is already the AetherBrowser backend the Chrome extension/PWA talks to (src/aetherbrowser/serve.py:5-8) and already exposes /health and a command-executing WebSocket; a maintainer wiring the Ops tab would plausibly add the subprocess endpoint here, and the very same token middleware would then be needed in a second app.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an ops route added next to the authenticated /v1/* routes but without the Depends(verify_api_key) dependency
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: api/main.py applies API-key auth per route via Depends(verify_api_key) (api/main.py:422-425, api/main.py:586) and leaves /v1/health open; a copy-paste of a route definition that drops the dependency is exactly the sibling shape a maintainer could write, and it would keep the ops guarantee broken in a second app at distance.

O9_family: CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function - unauthenticated access to operator/administrative endpoints (broken access control, operator data exposure)

O10_build.language: Python (FastAPI backend) plus an HTML/JS PWA page
O10_build.toolchain: pip/uv with fastapi, uvicorn, pydantic; pytest for tests
O10_build.project_tests: tests/aetherbrowser/ holds 22 test modules (e.g. tests/aetherbrowser/test_serve.py) covering the other AetherBrowser server, src/aetherbrowser/serve.py; no tests exist for scripts/aetherbrowser/api_server.py at the pinned commit because that module is absent.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard only the route the report names (POST /api/ops/check-email) with an inline header check, leaving the other /api/ops/* and /api/cli/* subprocess routes unauthenticated.

out_of_scope_notes: The same commit de7779 bundles unrelated protections outside this advisory: API keys are Fernet-encrypted at rest in src/api/stripe_billing.py (fix.diff:1395-1468) and scripts/hooks/pre-commit stops echoing matched secrets (fix.diff:1383-1394); neither is this advisory's ops-API protection, and the surrounding code is absent at the pinned commit (no _persist_key/_load_keys in src/api/stripe_billing.py, no scripts/hooks/pre-commit).

At the pinned commit a separate, unrelated AetherBrowser FastAPI app (src/aetherbrowser/serve.py) accepts WebSocket clients on /ws with no authentication and can drive provider execution (src/aetherbrowser/serve.py:65-67); not pursued because it is not the operator-digest sink and lies outside this advisory's protection.
unverified: repo_mb could not be measured (no shell): the tree has 1600+ Python files plus large JSONL training corpora, so tiny_repo is not claimed and giant_repo is not claimed either.

The fix diff's parent revision could not be identified (no shell/git): the pinned tree is demonstrably not that parent (no api_server.py, no scripts/hooks/pre-commit, no _persist_key in src/api/stripe_billing.py), so O1/O4/O8/O11 are measured against the pinned tree (0) while the fix diff's inventory is five /api/ops/* routes (fix.diff:1196, 1215, 1234, 1253, 1279) plus /api/cli/* (fix.diff:1356).
The real digest sink needs IMAP credentials and network (scripts/apollo/email_reader.py:166-173), so a hidden behavioural test would have to stub read_account; not exercised here.

Whether de7779's guard actually covers all subprocess routes in its own parent tree (e.g. /api/vault/sync at fix.diff:1161 or /api/red-team/run at fix.diff:905, both absent from _OPERATOR_PREFIXES) could not be confirmed against that tree, only against the fix diff.
